content:
Hi everyone! I’m a software engineer based in northern Ohio.

I’ve spent the last several years working in enterprise .NET environments, where I focus on system performance and building scalable infrastructure. Recently, I’ve been shifting my focus toward formal verification and the intersection of systems engineering and abstract logic.

I’ve been spending time getting familiar with CSLib, and I’m excited by the 'CS as infrastructure' mission. I recently put together a small fix for #638 (the HasWellFormed notation collision), which was a great way to learn the workflow and the CI requirements.

I’m currently in a ‘first-principles’ phase of study, working through some C++ kernel projects and reading quite a bit. I’ve been going through the CSLib whitepaper and am starting to dive into the papers on HML and the project’s infrastructure. My recent reading has kept me focused on the foundations of AI and formal verification, which has only deepened my interest in how we can formally verify these kinds of systems.

I’m here to learn and contribute. I want to deepen my involvement, but I’m very conscious of not stepping on any toes, especially with active proposals where the author is clearly already doing excellent work.

If there’s a particular corner of the Foundations or Computability modules that could use some extra hands, or if there’s a recurring 'paperwork' task that would free up time for the maintainers, I’d love to hear your thoughts. I’m eager to see where I can be most useful to the project.

Looking forward to meeting you all.
